corpus_crossquery.query: Which LEGEND safety or DDR statements could inherit stronger causality than PMID 26675548 directly demonstrates?
corpus_crossquery.finding: FT-060 and DIS-001 remain directionally supported, but ITCH inhibition risk must be described as a cross-paper mechanistic warning. PMID 26675548 directly supports WWOX ubiquitination, K274/WW1 dependence, p-ATM association, checkpoint phenotypes and a pleiotropic ATM-inhibitor response; it does not manipulate ITCH or establish K63 linkage within this study. DL-MECH-103 records the boundary.

retraction_check.result: No retraction, expression of concern or correction found for PMID 26675548.

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: Structured PMC XML and 12-page PDF are local and fingerprinted. Six native main-figure images were inspected. verbatim_locators.abstract_anchoring_waived: All textual locators below are from Results or Discussion, never the abstract; visual locators point to fingerprinted images.

entries.proposition: Early WWOX induction after damage is mainly post-translational, with delayed UVC-associated transcript induction.
entries.snippet: We found that WWOX expression, as assessed by real-time PCR, was upregulated 2 hours after UVC exposure but did not change after HU or APH treatment (Figure S2) suggesting that induction of WWOX at early time points is postranslationally regulated.
entries.anchor: Results, Effect of DNA single strand breaks on WWOX levels

entries.proposition: WWOX depletion attenuates CHK1 and H2AX checkpoint-associated phosphorylation after UVC.
entries.snippet: In contrast, MCF7-WWOX depleted cells (MCF7-shWWOX) show reduced activation of both proteins (p-CHK1 and γ-H2AX), suggesting a defect in the signalling pathway of ATR.
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX regulate DNA damage response checkpoint proteins following SSBs

entries.proposition: Wild-type WWOX, but not K274R, rescues checkpoint readouts in WWOX-depleted MCF7 cells.
entries.snippet: Restoration of WT form of WWOX, but not WWOXK274R, into MCF7-shWWOX could rescue the defect in ATR checkpoint activation upon DNA damage (Figure 2C).
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX regulate DNA damage response checkpoint proteins following SSBs

entries.proposition: WWOX depletion weakens the G2/M arrest after UVC.
entries.snippet: In contrast to control cells, which were readily arrested in G2, a significantly higher population of WWOX-depleted cells entered mitosis (Figure S5).
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX modulates the G2/M checkpoints following DNA damage

entries.proposition: Wwox-null MEFs have more APH-associated chromosome breaks than wild-type MEFs.
entries.snippet: Treatment of WT MEFs with 0.2 μM APH induced an average of ∼2.8 ± 1 chromosomal breaks whereas 5.7 ± 1.7 breaks were detectable in KO-MEFs (P<0.05) (Figure 3A, 3B, Figure S6A).
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX deficiency enhances chromosomal breaks upon DNA damage

entries.proposition: Wild-type WWOX rescue lowers the APH-associated break phenotype in knockout MEFs.
entries.snippet: Examination of metaphase spreads demonstrated that reconstitution of WWOX expression rescued the number of chromosomal breaks when compared to KO-Ad-GFP-infected and parental KO-MEFs (Figure 3D and Figure S6C).
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX deficiency enhances chromosomal breaks upon DNA damage

entries.proposition: Damage-associated ubiquitination is observed for wild-type WWOX but not K274R or WFPA in the transfected pull-down assay.
entries.snippet: Interestingly we found that WWOX also underwent ubiquitination following both UVC and HU treatment relative to control untreated cells (Figure 4C, upper panel line 1 vs. 3 and 4) but not the mutant form of K274R (line 5 vs. 7 and 8) or WFPA (line 9 vs. 11 and 12).
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX accumulation and ubiquitination following DNA damage

entries.proposition: GST-WWOX pull-downs contain p-ATM after replication-stress-associated treatments.
entries.snippet: As expected WWOX interacted with p-ATM following IR, but surprisingly, WWOX also associated with p-ATM following SSBs (Figure 5A).
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX associates with ATM following SSBs

entries.proposition: The ATM-inhibitor experiment reduces WWOX and multiple checkpoint proteins together rather than isolating one edge.
entries.snippet: Moreover, ATR downstream target p-CHK1 levels as well as ATM and its targets KAP1 and ITCH, were also reduced following ATM inhibition (Figure 5B).
entries.anchor: Results, WWOX modulates ATR checkpoint is ATM-dependent

entries.proposition: The authors acknowledge pleiotropy of ATM inhibition and leave other ATR-pathway targets possible.
entries.snippet: Nevertheless, we cannot exclude that WWOX could regulate other players in the ATR signaling pathway. It is also known that ATM inhibition results in pan changes that could affect DDR signalling; i.e increased levels of tumor suppressor ARF [48].
entries.anchor: Discussion, ATM dependence and model limitations

entries.proposition: Figure 1 shows rapid but non-monotonic WWOX protein induction across APH, HU and UVC conditions.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1A-C: WWOX fold-change values rise within 0.5-2 hours/minutes in MEF, HEK293T and MCF7 panels; several time courses later fall, including MEF UVC at 24 hours and HEK293T APH at 6 hours.

entries.proposition: Figure 2 visually supports checkpoint loss/rescue but relies on immunoblot comparisons rather than quantified effect sizes.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2A-C: p-CHK1 and γ-H2AX signals are weaker after WWOX depletion; wild-type WWOX rescue restores p-ATM, p-KAP1 and p-CHK1 more clearly than K274R. No densitometry or replicate count is displayed.
entries.anchor: Figure 2, panels A-C, native extracted PNG

entries.proposition: Figure 3 is the principal quantified functional endpoint and displays rescue of chromosome breaks.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 3A-D: metaphase images mark more breaks in KO; panel B plots approximately 2.8 versus 5.7 breaks/cell after APH with P<0.05; panel D shows KO-AdWWOX+APH approximately 1.9 versus KO-AdGFP+APH approximately 5.7, P<0.05.
entries.anchor: Figure 3, panels A-D, native extracted PNG

entries.proposition: Figure 4 shows fractionation and damage-associated ubiquitin signal but does not directly manipulate ITCH or identify K63 linkage.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 4A-C: WWOX increases in both nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions; HA-ubiquitin smear recovered with GST-WWOX increases after IR/UVC/HU and is weak with K274R/WFPA. No ITCH perturbation or K63-specific reagent appears in the panel.
entries.anchor: Figure 4, panels A-C, native extracted PNG

entries.proposition: Figure 5 supports association and inhibitor sensitivity but not clean genetic epistasis.
